guideTitle: Best Portable Power Stations for Camping (2026)
metaDescription: Portable power stations for camping compared on watt-hours, AC output, weight and recharge time, with honest runtime math for fridges, CPAPs and lights.
expertTake: The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 is the best overall pick because 1,024 Wh, 2,000 W of output and a 49 minute recharge claim cover a weekend of camping for most small families. The Jackery Explorer 300 is the value pick for lights, phones and a CPAP on short trips at a light 7.5 lb. Anyone who only needs to charge phones and a headlamp should skip power stations altogether and carry a power bank, which costs less and weighs far less.
introParagraphs: A portable power station is a big battery with an inverter, so you can run lights, a fridge, a laptop or a CPAP at the campsite without a generator. The key numbers are capacity in watt-hours, how many watts it can output at once, and how long it takes to recharge.

This guide compares power stations sized for camping, from compact 300 Wh units to 1,000 Wh class stations. We evaluated each on published specifications, capacity, output, weight, ports, charging speed and owner feedback patterns, and we show the runtime math so you can match a station to your gear.

products.name: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Power Station, 1,024 Wh, 2,000 W

specList.label: Recharge
specList.value: Full charge in 49 minutes at 1,600 W

products.description:
The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 pairs a 1,024 Wh LiFePO4 battery with 2,000 W of AC output, 3,000 W peak and ten ports. The maker claims a full recharge in 49 minutes using up to 1,600 W of input. It is a strong all-round camp station for a family or a campsite with a fridge and lights.

The fast recharge is the standout: a station that refills in under an hour from a wall outlet is easy to top up before a trip or in a car park. Compared with the EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic, it offers similar capacity and a slightly higher continuous output. Compared with the BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini, it is heavier and more powerful but less compact. It handles most camp appliances, including a small electric cooler, a laptop and lights.

In use, estimate runtime by dividing capacity by load, then subtract about 15 percent for inverter losses. A 60 W fridge cycles, so it draws less on average than its label. Heating appliances such as kettles and hair dryers drain a station quickly, so avoid them. Keep the station shaded and ventilated, and store it partly charged between trips.
products.bestFor: Families and car campers who want one station for a fridge, lights and laptops over a weekend.
pros: 1,024 Wh LiFePO4 capacity for multi-day use
2,000 W AC output runs most camp appliances
Claimed 49 minute full recharge
Ten ports cover AC, USB-C and car outputs
cons: Heavier and bulkier than 300 Wh class units
High-draw heaters still drain it quickly

products.name: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic, 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W AC, 3,600 W Surge
products.description:
The EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic is a 1,024 Wh station with 1,800 W of AC output and 3,600 W of surge, and a claimed charge from 0 to 80 percent in about 45 minutes. The surge rating helps with motors that draw a spike on startup, such as a compressor fridge. It is the main rival to the Anker C1000.

Compared with the Anker, its continuous output is a little lower, with a higher listed surge. Compared with the LIBRIDS C600, it has much more capacity and power, at a higher cost tier. The EcoFlow ecosystem adds app control and expansion options. It is a good fit if you want to power a camp kitchen with a small induction cooktop for short bursts.

Ownership notes: check the fan noise and the app, and keep the unit ventilated. Do not run it flat out for long in a hot tent. Charging from a car outlet is slower than wall charging, so plan your recharge. Store the station about half charged during long gaps, and check it every few months.
products.bestFor: Campers with a compressor fridge or higher-surge appliances who like app control.
pros: 1,800 W continuous with 3,600 W surge handles motor loads
0 to 80 percent in about 45 minutes claimed
1,024 Wh capacity for a weekend
App and ecosystem expansion options
cons: Heavy to carry far from the car
Surge rating does not extend run time

products.name: BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini, 1,004.8 Wh, 700 W LFP, 23.59 lb
products.description:
The BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini packs 1,004.8 Wh into a unit that weighs 23.59 lb and measures about 9.25 by 8.48 by 11.54 inches. The maker says it is 45 percent smaller and 36 percent lighter than a previous design, and lists idle consumption of under 10 W. AC output is 700 W, which limits what you can run.

The low output is the tradeoff: 700 W handles lights, laptops, a CPAP and a small fridge, but not a kettle or a microwave. Compared with the Anker C1000 or EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic, it has about the same capacity in a smaller and lighter package, but with much lower output. It is built for campers who prize carrying ease and low idle drain.

In practice, the low idle draw matters when you leave the inverter on overnight, because every watt of idle load eats stored energy. Estimate runtime with the same capacity-over-load math. The compact size fits a small car or a canoe. If you need to run a hot appliance, choose a higher-output station instead.
products.bestFor: Campers who want about 1 kWh in a compact, lighter case and have modest power needs.
pros: 1,004.8 Wh in a compact 23.59 lb body
Low idle consumption of under 10 W claimed
LFP battery chemistry per the listing
Fits small vehicles and tight storage
cons: Upper-mid cost tier for the output
Lower output than the 1 kWh rivals

products.name: LIBRIDS C600 Portable Power Station, 640 Wh, 600 W, 4 AC Outlets
products.description:
The LIBRIDS C600 offers 640 Wh with 600 W of AC output, 1,200 W of surge and eight output ports, including four AC outlets. It is a lesser-known brand positioned as a solar generator. It sits in the low to mid tier, between compact 300 Wh units and 1 kWh stations.

Four AC outlets are handy for a group, since you can power a lamp, a laptop charger and a small fridge at once. Compared with the Jackery Explorer 300, it has more than twice the capacity. Compared with the Anker C1000, it is smaller and cheaper, with much less capacity and output. It suits a weekend for two without a heavy electric load.

Ownership notes: the brand has a shorter track record, so check warranty and support terms. Keep the unit ventilated and use the manufacturer's charging cables. Runtime depends on load, and a 640 Wh unit runs a 50 W load for roughly ten hours after inverter losses. Check the solar input specifications before buying panels.
products.bestFor: Two or three campers who want multiple AC outlets and moderate capacity at a low to mid cost.
pros: 640 Wh capacity suits a weekend for two
Four AC outlets and eight ports in total
600 W rated output with 1,200 W surge
Low to mid cost tier
cons: Lesser-known brand with limited track record
Not enough for a hot appliance or a large fridge

products.name: Jackery Explorer 300 Power Station, 292 Wh, 7.5 lb

specList.label: Outlets
specList.value: 2 AC outlets, 100 W USB-C PD, USB-A and more

products.description:
The Jackery Explorer 300 stores 292 Wh in a 7.5 lb body and powers six devices through two AC outlets, a 100 W USB-C PD port and USB-A ports. It is the lightest and lowest cost station in this guide. It is a good fit for phones, lights, a laptop and a CPAP on a short trip.

The small capacity is its limit: 292 Wh runs a 30 W device for roughly eight hours after losses. Compared with the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2, it has similar capacity and weight, with a different brand and port layout. Compared with the LIBRIDS C600, it is much smaller. For someone who only needs light power at camp, it is the practical choice.

Ownership notes: if you use a CPAP, check its wattage, and turn off the humidifier to extend runtime. Avoid running anything with a heating element. Recharge before each trip, and store the unit partly charged. For one-night trips or kayak camping, the light weight is a real benefit.
products.bestFor: Short trips and light loads such as lights, phones, a laptop and a CPAP.
pros: Light 7.5 lb body is easy to carry
Two AC outlets, 100 W USB-C PD and USB-A ports
Lowest cost tier in the lineup
Established brand with wide support
cons: 292 Wh runs out quickly with larger loads

products.name: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Power Station, 288 Wh, 600 W, 9.4 lb

specList.label: AC output
specList.value: 600 W, with a 1,500 W power lifting mode

specList.label: Claim
specList.value: Twice the output of similar-capacity units

products.description:
The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 is a 288 Wh station that weighs 9.4 lb and offers 600 W of AC output, with a power lifting mode up to 1,500 W for some resistive loads. The maker says 600 W is twice as much as others in its class. It is aimed at storms and camping where a small unit must still run a real appliance.

The high output for the capacity is the draw, but capacity is what limits run time. Compared with the Jackery Explorer 300, it offers double the AC output at a similar capacity. Compared with the LIBRIDS C600, it is smaller, lighter and lower in capacity. Power lifting extends what it can run, but only for loads that behave simply, and it drains the battery quickly.

In use, plan runtime using capacity divided by load, and do not expect a hot appliance to run long. A 600 W load takes the 288 Wh to empty in well under half an hour. Use the unit for short, higher-power tasks, like a blender or a small tool, in addition to lights and phones. Keep it cool and charged.
products.bestFor: Campers who want a small, light station that can run an occasional higher-wattage item.
pros: 600 W AC output from a 9.4 lb unit
Power lifting mode for some higher loads
LFP chemistry per the listing
Easy to carry and store
cons: High loads drain the battery in minutes
Power lifting only suits certain appliances

buyingCriteria.explanation: Capacity tells you how long you can run a load. Divide watt-hours by the load in watts, then take about 85 percent for inverter losses. A 1,024 Wh unit like the Anker C1000 runs a 50 W load for roughly 17 hours, and a 292 Wh Jackery Explorer 300 runs it for about 5 hours. Estimate your gear first, because overbuying adds weight and cost.

Output in watts limits what you can run at once. The Elite 100 Mini lists 700 W, while the Anker C1000 lists 2,000 W and the EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic lists 1,800 W with 3,600 W surge. Motors, such as fridge compressors, draw a startup surge, so surge ratings matter. Heating appliances use huge power and are poor camp loads.

Power stations are heavy. The Jackery Explorer 300 weighs 7.5 lb, the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 weighs 9.4 lb and the Elite 100 Mini weighs 23.59 lb. A 1 kWh unit with high output is heavier still. If you carry it far from the car, weight dominates. Campsites near the car allow a larger station.

Wall charging speed varies, with claims such as 49 minutes for the Anker C1000 and 0 to 80 percent in 45 minutes for the EcoFlow. Car and solar charging are slower, and solar input depends on the panels. Check the maximum input for each source. A fast recharge helps if you can top up between trips.

LiFePO4 or LFP batteries last more charge cycles than older lithium types, which matters over years. The listings for the Anker, BLUETTI and LIBRIDS state LFP chemistry. Cycle life claims are maker figures. All lithium batteries should be stored partly charged and kept out of heat.

Check AC outlets, USB-C PD wattage and a car port. The LIBRIDS C600 has four AC outlets. Do not use power stations in enclosed tents with poor ventilation, and keep them away from fuel and heat. Power stations are not allowed on aircraft in most cases, because of their battery size. Follow the manual.

specDecoder.meaning: A lithium chemistry known for long cycle life and thermal stability, at some cost in weight.

specDecoder.meaning: The power the inverter uses while on with no load. It drains the battery overnight.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum power the station accepts when charging. Higher input means faster charging.

cards.label: Compact
cards.text: The Jackery Explorer 300, BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 and Elite 100 Mini are light and easy to carry, with limited output or capacity.

cards.label: High output
cards.text: The Anker C1000 and EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic power fridges and small appliances, but weigh more.

howToChoose.note: Choose compact for hikes from the car and light loads. Choose high output for a family car camp.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Watt-hours that match your loads, enough surge for motors, a weight you can carry and a recharge plan. Keep it shaded and ventilated.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Anker C1000 leads on power, the Elite 100 Mini on portability and the Jackery on weight.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You run a fridge, camp for several days or want fast recharge. The Anker or EcoFlow pays back in capacity.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only charge devices and run lights. A Jackery or BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 is enough.

maintenance.why: Lithium cells age faster when stored full or empty. Keep them around half charged.
Batteries self-discharge slowly. Charge to the recommended level.
Heat and moisture shorten battery life and affect safety. Store indoors.
Dust blocks cooling. Wipe the vents with a dry cloth.
Damaged cables are a fire and shock risk. Replace worn cables.

faq.q: How long will a power station run a fridge?
faq.a: Divide capacity by the fridge's average draw, then subtract losses. A compressor fridge cycles on and off, so average draw is lower than its label.
Usually yes. Check your CPAP's wattage and turn off the humidifier to extend runtime.

faq.q: Can I bring one on a plane?
faq.a: Generally no. Airlines restrict large lithium batteries, and most power stations exceed the limit.

faq.q: Is LFP better than other lithium?
faq.a: It offers longer cycle life and good thermal stability, but weighs more. Cycle life claims are maker figures.

faq.q: Can I use it in a tent?
faq.a: Power stations do not burn fuel, but keep them ventilated and out of heat. Follow the manual.
Not for a weekend if you can recharge at home. Solar helps on long trips, and input limits vary.
